> However, when looking at the metadata, `Base.foo` appears to have a `void` return type in the metadata.

An unspecified return type must be treated as a `Variant` if it is a newly declared method, or implicitly copy the return type from the parent method if it is an override.

The issue I'm running into is specific to generating dynamic scripts that extend a class.  I'm running into this issue in adapting [GUT](https://github.com/bitwes/Gut) (testing framework) to the improved return type checking Godot 4.7 does.

When GUT creates a double (a dynamic script generated at runtime that extends a class and overrides all methods in it) I now have to know when I can include `return` clauses.  In earlier versions of Godot the generated script could `return null` in all method overrides.  If I include that now, I get parser errors if the return type for the method is `-> void`.

It is still valid to include `return null` when a method does not have a return type declared (such a method that only has `pass` as the method body).  Code using the metadata to generate these overrides cannot detect the difference between a method that has `pass` as the body and one that has `->void` as the return type.

What GUT does is more complicated than just `return null`, but it gets the idea across.  I can give more detailed examples.  I was trying not to get too far into the details of how this is causing an issue in GUT.
